learning: Iteration 9 showed that cutting base_speed 1.5 to 1.3 raised slalom progress 0.34 to 0.51 and kept the oval at 20 of 20, while the s-bend dropped one finish. Speed is the only lever that has moved the slalom since geometry reached its limit. The next speed step tests whether the slalom keeps gaining or whether the s-bend cost is now too high.
notes: Geometry held at the iteration 8 and 9 best values. Only base_speed changes (1.3 to 1.2), so the slalom's response to speed can be read on a fixed platform.
rationale: Iteration 9 is the best measured design (681.3). Its base_speed cut from 1.5 to 1.3 lifted slalom progress from 0.34 to 0.51 and kept the oval at 20 of 20 (max_error 0.016). The s-bend fell from 19 to 18 finishes but kept line losses at 0.8 and oscillation at 0.28, under the 0.35 limit. The slalom is still at its max_error floor (0.064) with 1.1 line losses per run and low oscillation (0.23), so it reacts late on alternating bends rather than jittering. Speed is still the lever that moved the slalom, so the Builder's geometry is held identical to iteration 8 and 9 (body_length 0.10, mass 0.6, y 0.075, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.09). Controller: base_speed is lowered one more step to 1.2, with kp 2.8, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, antisymmetric weights and last_direction unchanged, so the speed effect can be read alone. The oval's mean finish time (1.75 s at 1.5 and at 1.3) leaves margin under the 3 s limit. Expected, not measured: slalom progress above 0.51, with the s-bend holding 17 or more finishes. Risk: if the s-bend falls below 17 finishes, speed is now costing bend time, so return to 1.3.
